headline: Majors overbought and crowded long into a week of heavy whale selling, funding at 11% annualized and longs liquidating on stops.
paragraphs: All six tracked majors sit above their 200-day moving averages, but none have closed above the 50-day yet; no golden crosses exist in the set. That means the trend is up but the acceleration phase has not confirmed. Bitcoin and Ethereum are up 23.85% and 39.09% over the last month, yet they sit 36.7% and 47.5% below their 12-month highs respectively. Ethereum is the outlier momentum machine: RSI 80.3 and volatility at 70.1% tells you it has moved fast and hard. Cardano alone sits below its 200-day, a single crack in the otherwise unified up-trend. The picture is a rally in progress, not a new leg confirmed.

Momentum has run into overbought territory across the board. Bitcoin RSI at 82.1, Ethereum at 80.3, Solana at 84.9, XRP at 85.3, BNB at 84.8, and Doge at 83.6 are all in the top decile of the 0-to-100 range. MACD is above signal on every single asset, so the price bars are still rising faster than their averages, but when five of seven majors exceed RSI 83, the move has no room left to accelerate without a rest. Cardano at RSI 73.1 is the only one with air left. This is the tape of a crowd that has already bet the momentum turn; the question is whether price can keep carrying it or whether it needs to pause.

Funding sits at 0.01% per 8-hour period (11% annualized) across all tracked assets on OKX, which is not extreme but is material enough that longs are paying to hold. The real signal lives in positioning: Bitcoin open interest is 2.34 billion, Ethereum 1.46 billion, Solana 272 million. The long-short ratios tell a tighter story. Bitcoin shows 1.1 longs per short, Ethereum 1.15, reasonable and balanced. But Solana hits 1.97, XRP 2.14, and Doge 3.21 longs per short. That is a crowded long book in the smaller caps; one hard stop and the liquidation cascade runs one way. In the last 24 hours across four hours for Bitcoin and 13 for Ethereum, liquidations have favored shorts: 10.7 million of Bitcoin shorts liquidated against 1.8 million longs, 10.9 million Ethereum shorts against 2.7 million longs. That is the mark of the late-stage buyer paying up to stop out bears. Solana flipped the pattern, with 4.3 million longs liquidated against 1.6 million shorts, a sign the leverage chase has begun to turn. The boat is full and the price has room to hurt people.

Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows Bitcoin moving off exchanges (88.4 million out via Kraken alone), classic accumulation behavior when the crowd is hot. Over the longer window, the pattern shifts: week ending August 3rd saw 972 million move off exchanges, but the last three weeks show 42 million, 473 million, and 1.091 billion moving back onto exchanges. That is a steady retreat from cold storage into trade, a signal that holders are trimming into the rally. Against this, stablecoin float stands flat at 308.5 billion, up 0.01% over the month, meaning dry powder has not been deployed to chase the move; instead, the existing capital is recycling. Bitcoin spot ETFs took 307.5 million on August 21st and 1.92 billion net over the last five sessions, all five days positive. That traditional-finance bid is consistent but modest relative to the crypto move itself.

The Fear and Greed gauge reads 73 (Greed), near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 73, confirming what the tape shows: the crowd is confident. Yet the crowd is also taking chips off the table (exchangeward flows) while the leverage class is paying 11% to carry bets that are already far from their peaks. Sentiment and action are diverging quietly. Bitcoin dominance sits at 58.9%, stable, suggesting flows are distributed rather than herding into a single name.

Watch for three conditions. First, the 50-day reclaim: if either Bitcoin or Ethereum close above the 50-day moving average, the golden cross becomes live and a new uptrend formally confirms. Second, funding flip: if 8-hour rates turn negative (shorts paying longs), the carry has reversed and late buyers have paid peak fee. Third, liquidation reversal: if long liquidations begin to exceed shorts across Bitcoin and Ethereum at scale, the stop orders have started to trigger and pain has shifted to the bulls. The rally is real but overbought; the question is whether the late-stage price action absorbs the wheel churn or spins it.
